extraction.body: The Social Security cost-of-living adjustment will be 3.6% in 2027, the Social Security Administration said on Wednesday. The cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA, provides an annual inflation adjustment to both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, benefits. Social Security retirement benefits will increase by $75 per month on average, the agency said. "Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability," Social Security Commissioner Frank Bisignano said in a statement. Around 72 million Social Security recipients will see the benefit increases in January, according to SSA. About 7.3 million SSI beneficiaries will receive higher payments starting Dec. 31, the agency said. The 3.6% COLA for 2027 is in line with Social Security experts' projections , which last month forecast an increase of 3.5% to 3.6%. The 3.6% COLA for 2027 is the largest increase to benefits since 2023. That year, beneficiaries received an 8.7% benefit boost — the highest in four decades — in response to rising inflation. New government inflation data released on Wednesday shows consumer price increases are accelerating. The consumer price index rose 3.7% over the past 12 months, as gas prices jumped. About 40% of Social Security beneficiaries ages 65 and over rely on the program for at least half of their income, according to the AARP . A recent AARP survey found 76% of respondents said a 3.5% COLA would not be enough . The Social Security COLA is "critically important" because it helps millions of Americans cover rising everyday costs, including groceries, routine bills and health care, AARP CEO Myechia Minter-Jordan said in a statement. "There's a lot on the line financially right now for older Americans: one in five have no retirement savings, and more people feel financially insecure this year than last," Minter-Jordan said. Beneficiaries can multiply their current monthly benefit amount by 3.6%, or 0.036, to estimate the increase to their checks for 2027. However, keep in mind that increases to Medicare Part B or Part D premiums for 2027 — which may be deducted directly from benefit checks — can affect the size of beneficiaries' monthly payments. Standard monthly premiums for Medicare Part B are projected to be $209.50 in 2027 , up from $202.90 in 2026, according to a report from Medicare trustees. Some beneficiaries may pay extra surcharges, known as Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amounts, or IRMAAs, if they have higher incomes. Medicare Part B covers medically necessary and preventive services. Meanwhile, Medicare Part D prescription drug plans may see modest premium increases in 2027, according to an analysis by KFF , a nonpartisan health policy research group. The Social Security Administration will send beneficiaries notices about the COLA changes. The notices will include specific information about their 2027 benefits, including exact payment dates and dollar amounts, as well as any deductions. Individuals who have created online My Social Security accounts can access that information starting in late November, according to the agency. Beneficiaries without an online account who want to see their COLA notice online must create an account and opt into paperless notices by Nov. 18. Beneficiaries who have not signed up to receive online notices will receive mailed COLA statements in December. Those individuals should make sure the address the agency has on file is up to date, according to SSA. Medicare premium amounts for 2027 will also be available online through the My Social Security message center starting in late November, the agency said. The COLA is based on the percentage increase of one specific government inflation measure — the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, or CPI-W — from the third quarter of the previous year to the third quarter of the current year. The CPI-W is a subset of the consumer price index that tracks the average change in prices for goods and services purchased by urban households. The CPI-W rose 3.9% over the past 12 months, according to September data the Bureau of Labor Statistics released on Wednesday. Policymakers and advocates have proposed alternatives to the CPI-W for calculating the annual COLA. One alternative is the chained CPI, an index that accounts for changes in buying habits as prices rise. However, a recent AARP analysis found that switching to that measure would "substantially lower benefits over time." Others have proposed using the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly, or CPI-E, an experimental index that tracks spending for individuals ages 62 and over. However, some experts say the CPI-E does not necessarily grow much faster than the current measure used to calculate benefit increases. Switching to a different COLA measure is among the changes lawmakers may consider in upcoming Social Security reform. "Social Security's future is on the ballot this November, and that includes the size of annual COLA adjustments," said Nancy Altman, president of Social Security Works, an advocacy group focused on expanding Social Security. passages: How the COLA is calculated matters: the Social Security Administration uses the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) to set the COLA, comparing the average CPI-W in the third quarter to the third quarter a year earlier.
Advocacy-group projections translate current monthly CPI releases into a preliminary COLA estimate; AARP published its 3.6% figure by analyzing those inflation series.
Advocacy groups have converged on a roughly 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 after recent government inflation releases.
AARP’s estimate says beneficiaries could see a 3.6% increase next year, based on current CPI measures, and The Senior Citizens League’s updated projection also puts the 2027 COLA near 3.6%.
Financial coverage and analysts have echoed the advocacy-group estimates.
One internal analysis noted the official 2027 COLA will be announced on Oct.

Coverage from Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool discussed that a higher COLA increases benefits and program outlays, while also reflecting broader inflation trends that affect seniors’ purchasing power.

That said, reports indicated that Apple would release a refreshed HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K first, and that the companies first smart home hub (otherwise known as HomePod with Display or HomePad) might debut a little bit later. The company is already planning an upgraded Apple TV set-top box and a new HomePod mini for this time frame. But the scale of the retail changes suggests something else is coming: the long-anticipated home hub with a display. The planned modifications appear too extensive to be solely about routine updates to existing products. Of course, we’ll never know for certain until Apple holds its September keynote. Based on today’s reporting though, it sounds like we might get our first glimpse at Apple’s all-new smart home hub quite soon, alongside refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini models that should support Siri AI. As a refresher, Apple’s smart home hub is rumored to sport a 7-inch square display and come in two versions: one with a built in speaker, and another with magnets on the rear that’ll support wall mounting. sources.title: Apple launches HomeView: Here’s what the $299 Siri AI smart home hub can do - The News International
passages: Apple has unveiled HomeView, a new AI-powered smart home hub featuring a seven-inch screen, facial recognition and upgraded Siri capabilities.
Apple said its upgraded Siri AI can answer questions and hold conversations that users can continue on their iPhones or iPads.

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home,” Apple's marketing chief Greg Joswiak said.
The launches mark Apple's second major product event under CEO John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook in September.
The device also supports FaceTime calls, music playback and smart home controls, allowing users to monitor security cameras, adjust thermostats and lock doors.
The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K priced at $299 and an updated HomePod Mini costing $149.
HomeView can be mounted on a wall or placed on a table and supports up to six household members
The device, announced on Tuesday, will cost $299 and become available on November 13, according to CNBC.

sources.title: Apple launches HomeView: Here’s what the $299 Siri AI smart home hub can do - The News International
passages: Apple has unveiled HomeView, a new AI-powered smart home hub featuring a seven-inch screen, facial recognition and upgraded Siri capabilities.
Apple said its upgraded Siri AI can answer questions and hold conversations that users can continue on their iPhones or iPads.

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home,” Apple's marketing chief Greg Joswiak said.
The launches mark Apple's second major product event under CEO John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook in September.
The device also supports FaceTime calls, music playback and smart home controls, allowing users to monitor security cameras, adjust thermostats and lock doors.
The company also announced a new Apple TV 4K priced at $299 and an updated HomePod Mini costing $149.
HomeView can be mounted on a wall or placed on a table and supports up to six household members
The device, announced on Tuesday, will cost $299 and become available on November 13, according to CNBC.

Strategy’s new willingness to sell Bitcoin as well as buy it removes the assumption that the largest corporate holder is a one-way buyer, adding a potential source of supply in weaker markets. On the positive side, regulatory guidance from US agencies has eased a key overhang. Bitcoin still has to compete for capital with AI stocks and with Treasury yields that have risen sharply this year, so a turn lower in yields after US inflation data would be the clearest macro tailwind for his $100,000 call. Saylor is talking his book, but his core pitch, that AI makes scarcity more valuable, is an argument worth weighing on its merits. Strategy co-founder and executive chairman Michael Saylor said Bitcoin is entering a new bull market and should climb back above $100,000, arguing that artificial intelligence will push investors towards assets whose supply cannot be expanded. Speaking to Bloomberg Television at DC Fintech Week on Tuesday, Saylor said Bitcoin bottomed slightly below $60,000 during the past year’s contraction and has since rebounded into the $80,000s. He declined to give a timeframe for his $100,000 target, saying he plans in centuries, not months. Strategy’s longer-term forecast is for Bitcoin to grow 20% to 30% a year over the next two decades. At the heart of his case is scarcity. Saylor argued that AI will reduce the value of companies built on large human workforces or on chasing the next breakthrough product, while increasing demand for scarce capital such as Palm Beach real estate, gold and Bitcoin. In his words, investors will look for things robots cannot make more of. The argument has some logic. If AI makes labour and software abundant, assets with fixed supply could gain relative appeal. But it comes from the executive chairman of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with a stake he put at more than $70 billion. Bloomberg’s interviewers also challenged it, noting that AI is absorbing much of the market’s capital and that the scarcity rotation has yet to show clearly in Bitcoin, which remains about 30% below last year’s record high. Saylor countered that since Strategy began buying in August 2020, Bitcoin has returned about 38% a year and the company’s shares more than 50% a year, outpacing gold and every Magnificent Seven stock except Nvidia. By his own description, Bitcoin is also a volatile asset, with volatility of around 40, while Strategy’s shares run at roughly 80. He pointed to new tailwinds: favourable US regulation, faster bank adoption, the spread of tokenised securities and the growth of digital credit. He said the Senate’s failure to advance the Clarity Act was the best outcome for the industry, as guidance from the Treasury, the SEC and the CFTC proved more supportive than the bill’s restrictions. Saylor also defended Strategy’s sale of a small amount of Bitcoin in June, when prices were around $73,000, a move that unsettled the market. He described the company as a structured finance business that must be able to buy or sell Bitcoin, equity or credit as conditions require, mainly to support dividends on its credit products. He said those products pay 10% to 12% treated as a return of capital, which defers tax, and that the company expects to keep increasing its Bitcoin holdings in a bull market. MSCI is due to decide on Friday whether to exclude companies like Strategy from its global indices on the grounds they mainly accumulate assets. Saylor called the proposal a bad precedent, argued Strategy is an operating company like banks and insurers, and said the decision was not that important to the firm. Explainer: MSCI, Strategy and the index question What is MSCI? MSCI is one of the world’s largest index providers. Its benchmarks, such as the MSCI World and MSCI USA, are tracked by trillions of dollars in pension funds, ETFs and other investment products. When a company joins or leaves an MSCI index, funds that track it generally have to buy or sell the shares, whatever their view of the company. What is Strategy? Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy and listed under the ticker MSTR, started as an enterprise software company. Since August 2020 it has focused on buying and holding Bitcoin, funded largely by issuing shares, debt and preferred-style securities. It is now the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, with holdings Saylor puts at more than $70 billion. What are “digital credit” products? These are Strategy’s income-paying securities, such as STRC, backed by the company’s Bitcoin holdings. Saylor says they pay 10% to 12% a year, treated as a return of capital, which generally defers tax rather than removing it. The company may sell Bitcoin or other assets to fund these payments, which is why it now says it must be free to sell as well as buy. What is MSCI considering? MSCI has been reviewing whether companies whose main activity is accumulating digital assets, often called digital asset treasury companies, should stay in its global equity indices. It is assessing whether these firms are operating businesses or are closer to investment vehicles, which index providers often exclude. Why does it matter? Exclusion could force index-tracking funds to sell Strategy shares, putting pressure on the stock and potentially on the company’s ability to raise money. It would also set a precedent for the growing number of similar companies. Saylor argues Strategy is an operating company comparable to banks and insurers, since it creates and sells credit products. He says the decision is not that important to the firm. What happens next? MSCI is due to announce its decision on Friday, October 16. A decision to exclude would typically take effect at a later index review, giving funds time to adjust. Strategy’s new willingness to sell Bitcoin as well as buy it removes the assumption that the largest corporate holder is a one-way buyer, adding a potential source of supply in weaker markets. On the positive side, regulatory guidance from US agencies has eased a key overhang. Bitcoin still has to compete for capital with AI stocks and with Treasury yields that have risen sharply this year, so a turn lower in yields after US inflation data would be the clearest macro tailwind for his $100,000 call. Saylor is talking his book, but his core pitch, that AI makes scarcity more valuable, is an argument worth weighing on its merits. Strategy co-founder and executive chairman Michael Saylor said Bitcoin is entering a new bull market and should climb back above $100,000, arguing that artificial intelligence will push investors towards assets whose supply cannot be expanded. Speaking to Bloomberg Television at DC Fintech Week on Tuesday, Saylor said Bitcoin bottomed slightly below $60,000 during the past year’s contraction and has since rebounded into the $80,000s. He declined to give a timeframe for his $100,000 target, saying he plans in centuries, not months. Strategy’s longer-term forecast is for Bitcoin to grow 20% to 30% a year over the next two decades. At the heart of his case is scarcity. Saylor argued that AI will reduce the value of companies built on large human workforces or on chasing the next breakthrough product, while increasing demand for scarce capital such as Palm Beach real estate, gold and Bitcoin. In his words, investors will look for things robots cannot make more of. The argument has some logic. If AI makes labour and software abundant, assets with fixed supply could gain relative appeal. But it comes from the executive chairman of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with a stake he put at more than $70 billion. Bloomberg’s interviewers also challenged it, noting that AI is absorbing much of the market’s capital and that the scarcity rotation has yet to show clearly in Bitcoin, which remains about 30% below last year’s record high. Saylor countered that since Strategy began buying in August 2020, Bitcoin has returned about 38% a year and the company’s shares more than 50% a year, outpacing gold and every Magnificent Seven stock except Nvidia. By his own description, Bitcoin is also a volatile asset, with volatility of around 40, while Strategy’s shares run at roughly 80. He pointed to new tailwinds: favourable US regulation, faster bank adoption, the spread of tokenised securities and the growth of digital credit. He said the Senate’s failure to advance the Clarity Act was the best outcome for the industry, as guidance from the Treasury, the SEC and the CFTC proved more supportive than the bill’s restrictions. Saylor also defended Strategy’s sale of a small amount of Bitcoin in June, when prices were around $73,000, a move that unsettled the market. He described the company as a structured finance business that must be able to buy or sell Bitcoin, equity or credit as conditions require, mainly to support dividends on its credit products. He said those products pay 10% to 12% treated as a return of capital, which defers tax, and that the company expects to keep increasing its Bitcoin holdings in a bull market. MSCI is due to decide on Friday whether to exclude companies like Strategy from its global indices on the grounds they mainly accumulate assets. Saylor called the proposal a bad precedent, argued Strategy is an operating company like banks and insurers, and said the decision was not that important to the firm. Explainer: MSCI, Strategy and the index question What is MSCI? MSCI is one of the world’s largest index providers. Its benchmarks, such as the MSCI World and MSCI USA, are tracked by trillions of dollars in pension funds, ETFs and other investment products. When a company joins or leaves an MSCI index, funds that track it generally have to buy or sell the shares, whatever their view of the company. What is Strategy? Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy and listed under the ticker MSTR, started as an enterprise software company. Since August 2020 it has focused on buying and holding Bitcoin, funded largely by issuing shares, debt and preferred-style securities. It is now the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, with holdings Saylor puts at more than $70 billion. What are “digital credit” products? These are Strategy’s income-paying securities, such as STRC, backed by the company’s Bitcoin holdings. Saylor says they pay 10% to 12% a year, treated as a return of capital, which generally defers tax rather than removing it. The company may sell Bitcoin or other assets to fund these payments, which is why it now says it must be free to sell as well as buy. What is MSCI considering? MSCI has been reviewing whether companies whose main activity is accumulating digital assets, often called digital asset treasury companies, should stay in its global equity indices. It is assessing whether these firms are operating businesses or are closer to investment vehicles, which index providers often exclude. Why does it matter? Exclusion could force index-tracking funds to sell Strategy shares, putting pressure on the stock and potentially on the company’s ability to raise money. It would also set a precedent for the growing number of similar companies. Saylor argues Strategy is an operating company comparable to banks and insurers, since it creates and sells credit products. He says the decision is not that important to the firm. What happens next? MSCI is due to announce its decision on Friday, October 16. A decision to exclude would typically take effect at a later index review, giving funds time to adjust. passages: Friday’s upcoming MSCI decision on whether to exclude companies like Strategy from its global indices is the nearest catalyst, since an exclusion could trigger passive selling of the shares even if Saylor plays down its importance. Strategy’s new willingness to sell Bitcoin as well as buy it removes the assumption that the largest corporate holder is a one-way buyer, adding a potential source of supply in weaker markets. On the positive side, regulatory guidance from US agencies has eased a key overhang. Bitcoin still has to compete for capital with AI stocks and with Treasury yields that have risen sharply this year, so a turn lower in yields after US inflation data would be the clearest macro tailwind for his $100,000 call.
Saylor is talking his book, but his core pitch, that AI makes scarcity more valuable, is an argument worth weighing on its merits.

Strategy co-founder and executive chairman Michael Saylor said Bitcoin is entering a new bull market and should climb back above $100,000, arguing that artificial intelligence will push investors towards assets whose supply cannot be expanded.

Speaking to Bloomberg Television at DC Fintech Week on Tuesday, Saylor said Bitcoin bottomed slightly below $60,000 during the past year’s contraction and has since rebounded into the $80,000s. He declined to give a timeframe for his $100,000 target, saying he plans in centuries, not months. Strategy’s longer-term forecast is for Bitcoin to grow 20% to 30% a year over the next two decades.

At the heart of his case is scarcity. Saylor argued that AI will reduce the value of companies built on large human workforces or on chasing the next breakthrough product, while increasing demand for scarce capital such as Palm Beach real estate, gold and Bitcoin. In his words, investors will look for things robots cannot make more of.

The argument has some logic. If AI makes labour and software abundant, assets with fixed supply could gain relative appeal. But it comes from the executive chairman of the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holder, with a stake he put at more than $70 billion. Bloomberg’s interviewers also challenged it, noting that AI is absorbing much of the market’s capital and that the scarcity rotation has yet to show clearly in Bitcoin, which remains about 30% below last year’s record high.

Saylor countered that since Strategy began buying in August 2020, Bitcoin has returned about 38% a year and the company’s shares more than 50% a year, outpacing gold and every Magnificent Seven stock except Nvidia. By his own description, Bitcoin is also a volatile asset, with volatility of around 40, while Strategy’s shares run at roughly 80.

He pointed to new tailwinds: favourable US regulation, faster bank adoption, the spread of tokenised securities and the growth of digital credit. He said the Senate’s failure to advance the Clarity Act was the best outcome for the industry, as guidance from the Treasury, the SEC and the CFTC proved more supportive than the bill’s restrictions.

Saylor also defended Strategy’s sale of a small amount of Bitcoin in June, when prices were around $73,000, a move that unsettled the market. He described the company as a structured finance business that must be able to buy or sell Bitcoin, equity or credit as conditions require, mainly to support dividends on its credit products. He said those products pay 10% to 12% treated as a return of capital, which defers tax, and that the company expects to keep increasing its Bitcoin holdings in a bull market.

MSCI is due to decide on Friday whether to exclude companies like Strategy from its global indices on the grounds they mainly accumulate assets. Saylor called the proposal a bad precedent, argued Strategy is an operating company like banks and insurers, and said the decision was not that important to the firm.
Explainer: MSCI, Strategy and the index question

What is MSCI? MSCI is one of the world’s largest index providers. Its benchmarks, such as the MSCI World and MSCI USA, are tracked by trillions of dollars in pension funds, ETFs and other investment products. When a company joins or leaves an MSCI index, funds that track it generally have to buy or sell the shares, whatever their view of the company.

What is Strategy? Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy and listed under the ticker MSTR, started as an enterprise software company. Since August 2020 it has focused on buying and holding Bitcoin, funded largely by issuing shares, debt and preferred-style securities. It is now the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, with holdings Saylor puts at more than $70 billion.

What are “digital credit” products? These are Strategy’s income-paying securities, such as STRC, backed by the company’s Bitcoin holdings. Saylor says they pay 10% to 12% a year, treated as a return of capital, which generally defers tax rather than removing it. The company may sell Bitcoin or other assets to fund these payments, which is why it now says it must be free to sell as well as buy.

What is MSCI considering? MSCI has been reviewing whether companies whose main activity is accumulating digital assets, often called digital asset treasury companies, should stay in its global equity indices. It is assessing whether these firms are operating businesses or are closer to investment vehicles, which index providers often exclude.

Why does it matter? Exclusion could force index-tracking funds to sell Strategy shares, putting pressure on the stock and potentially on the company’s ability to raise money. It would also set a precedent for the growing number of similar companies. Saylor argues Strategy is an operating company comparable to banks and insurers, since it creates and sells credit products. He says the decision is not that important to the firm.
What happens next? MSCI is due to announce its decision on Friday, October 16. A decision to exclude would typically take effect at a later index review, giving funds time to adjust.

His view offers a sharp contrast with the pressures he said had weighed on prices in recent months. Saylor cited restrictive trade, foreign, currency and monetary policies as headwinds, while pointing to a more favorable regulatory environment, faster bank adoption, tokenized securities and growth in the digital asset market as potential support. Saylor said Bitcoin was trading 25% above its two-hundred-week moving average after briefly dipping below it. He also described the development of digital credit networks and the arrival of banking credit as favorable for the asset. “We've got the formation of and the strengthening of digital credit networks and, of course, banking credit coming online, and all these things are very auspicious for the asset,” he said. The forecast matters to investors because it links Saylor’s optimism to a mix of market structure and policy conditions, rather than price momentum alone. But the figures remain his outlook, not a guarantee of future performance. “I think that it should definitely move back into the six figures, back beyond $100,000,” Saylor said. Strategy’s own trading policy also featured in the interview. Saylor said buying and selling Bitcoin is part of the company’s regular financial activity, alongside transactions involving dollars, equity, credit, STRC and its own shares. He argued that the company needs flexibility to move among those assets and sources of capital. Saylor said that refusing to sell equity, capital or credit could degrade the company’s value, and described the ability to trade different asset pairs in either direction as a major unlock for investors. The company also repurchased 1.9 million STRC shares for $192.4 million. Investor sentiment on Stocktwits was weak: retail sentiment around MSTR fell from “bearish” to “extremely bearish” over 24 hours amid low message volumes, while sentiment around BTC was “bearish,” also with low message volumes. sources.title: Apple releases HomeView smart home hub with screen as showcase for Siri AI - CNBC
passages: Apple said its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
Apple on Tuesday announced a home hub called HomeView, marking CEO John Ternus' first launch outside of iPhones since he took over from Tim Cook at the start of September.
Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad.

"It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement.
The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch.

The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month.
Apple is emphasizing privacy, and said on Tuesday that its Apple Home Collection accessories encrypt data so that only the user and people they share with can see it.
Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers.
Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence.
People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone.

"Apple always waits for an ecosystem to develop first until they are positive they can provide a stellar user experience," said Jennifer Kent, principal analyst at Parks Associates, which conducts research on the connected home.
Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday.
Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price.
Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories.
But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage.
It also comes as Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster.

Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers.
Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence.
People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone.

Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories.
But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage.
It also comes as Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster.

Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple said its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
Apple on Tuesday announced a home hub called HomeView, marking CEO John Ternus' first launch outside of iPhones since he took over from Tim Cook at the start of September.
Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad.

"It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's marketing head Greg Joswiak said in a statement.
The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch.

The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month.
Apple is emphasizing privacy, and said on Tuesday that its Apple Home Collection accessories encrypt data so that only the user and people they share with can see it.
Other smart home cameras, for example, maintain limited access to user video, or store it on servers.
Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence.
People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone.

"Apple always waits for an ecosystem to develop first until they are positive they can provide a stellar user experience," said Jennifer Kent, principal analyst at Parks Associates, which conducts research on the connected home.
Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday.
Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price.
Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories.
But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage.
It also comes as Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster.

Prices start at $299 with pre-orders opened and shipments starting November 13.

The 7-inch device combines touch controls for lights, locks and cameras with FaceTime, speakers, personalized household screens and Siri AI. The launch gives Apple a direct answer to screen-equipped home hubs from Amazon and Google, a category where Apple has largely relied on iPads, HomePods and third-party accessories. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people, while its most sensitive personalized functions require an eligible, nearby and recently unlocked iPhone or iPad. According to Apple’s HomeView announcement , the device has a 7-inch Liquid Retina display and an A18 chip. It is available as a tabletop model or a wall-mounted model, both listed at $299 in the United States. The wall version requires a separate Schneider Home mount. Apple lists USB-C and AC-wired mounts at $59.95 and $79.95, respectively, while a Power over Ethernet mount priced at $129.95 is not expected until early 2027. Apple says HomeView can recognize up to six people and show personalized calendars, reminders, photo collections and home controls. CNBC’s launch coverage also describes the device as a showcase for the company’s Siri AI effort and household-profile system. Recognition does not by itself open a person’s private material. Apple says personal content requires that user’s paired iPhone or iPad to be nearby and recently unlocked. Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. Apple describes HomeView as a shared device for household tasks while keeping personal content tied to a user’s paired device. Apple also says camera and microphone information is processed in protected hardware runtimes unavailable to HomeView software, apps, users or Apple itself. The company presents those protections as part of its privacy approach. HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories. Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri. Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. The release does not provide a service-by-service list or clearly state which video apps run directly on HomeView and which require an iPhone, iPad or another Apple device. WIRED’s hands-on report says HomeView has no App Store and that YouTube, Netflix and Disney+ were not available as native apps at the time of its briefing. AppleInsider reported that video playback may depend on AirPlay from an iPhone or iPad or on CarPlay-related functionality. The available reporting does not resolve which services Apple considers compatible video apps. Preorders began Oct. 13 in the first group of markets. Apple says Singapore preorders begin Oct. 15. South Africa is scheduled to receive HomeView on Nov. 13 through authorized resellers. Apple says HomeView will not be sold in the European Union at launch because Siri AI is unavailable in iOS there. Siri AI is labeled beta in HomeView software version 27.2, and Apple says its personal-context capabilities require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. HomeView becomes available Nov. 13 in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The launch gives Apple a direct answer to screen-equipped home hubs from Amazon and Google, a category where Apple has largely relied on iPads, HomePods and third-party accessories.
Apple also says camera and microphone information is processed in protected hardware runtimes unavailable to HomeView software, apps, users or Apple itself.
Apple is also using HomeView to promote its Apple Home Collection, a group of accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
CNET’s launch coverage cites Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, saying Apple has made setup for the new home products simpler than alternatives that require separate apps and QR-code scanning.
Personal-context Siri requests also require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.
Apple describes HomeView as a shared device for household tasks while keeping personal content tied to a user’s paired device.
HomeView is a touch-and-voice controller for compatible Apple Home and Matter accessories.
Apple says users can view as many as nine live camera feeds at once and control connected devices through the screen or Siri.
The release does not provide a service-by-service list or clearly state which video apps run directly on HomeView and which require an iPhone, iPad or another Apple device.

passages: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.

extraction.body: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView , designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2 Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13. “Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.” HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable. The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer. A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation. A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests. Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer. With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro. With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery. With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant. Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments. HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement. HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts, Apple News, 4 Apple TV, and compatible third-party audio and video apps. 5 With Handoff, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio. HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking. With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods charging case, or personal item with an AirTag attached. With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it. 7 Offering added peace of mind, HomeView also detects the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and alerts users on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 11 and designed to be recycled. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.
HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts®, Apple News®, 4 Apple TV®, and compatible third-party audio and video apps.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod®, HomePod mini®, and AirPlay®-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud® to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac®, Apple Watch®, or Apple Vision Pro®.

extraction.body: Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core Apple® today introduced Apple HomeView™, designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina® display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime® calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core. 1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My®. HomeView features Siri® AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence™-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses. 2 Powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, Apple HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place. Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13. “Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.” HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable. The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone®, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer. A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation. A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests. Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer. With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone® or iPad®, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music®, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before. 3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud® to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac®, Apple Watch®, or Apple Vision Pro®. With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery. With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant. Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments. HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement. HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts®, Apple News®, 4 Apple TV®, and compatible third-party audio and video apps. 5 With Handoff®, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod®, HomePod mini®, and AirPlay®-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio. HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage® keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room. 6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking. With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods® charging case, or personal item with an AirTag® attached. And with Live Activities®, HomeView surfaces timely, at-a-glance information, like the song that’s currently playing, an active timer, or an incoming Intercom message from another room. HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds. The Home Modular face offers instant access to users’ favorite accessories, while the Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds at once, letting users keep an eye on doorstep deliveries and pets playing in the yard. With a supported iCloud+® subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door. With video descriptions for HomeKit® Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it. 7 Offering added peace of mind, HomeView also detects the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and alerts users on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection™ — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories. 8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more. 9 Like every Apple product, HomeView was built with privacy and security at its core. HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system. Isolation features added across many core components of the silicon work in tandem to protect Secure Exclaves and keep them segregated from the rest of the system. Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple. To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked. 10 Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud. When processed in Private Cloud Compute, data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else. HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 11 and designed to be recycled. Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it. coreStoryFacts.text: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home

“It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home.

And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”

With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.
By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.

HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.
With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030.

HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets.
HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry.
HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system.
Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple.

To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio.
A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension.
Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud.

HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds.
Apple® today introduced Apple HomeView™, designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it.

passages: Billions in Defense Modernization Are Driving Demand for Advanced AI, Autonomous Coordination, and Next-Generation Battlefield IntelligenceNEW YORK, Oct.
14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out.

As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself.
That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in.

By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively.
Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030.

For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical.

Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV), Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ: ONDS), AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV), UiPath, Inc. (NYSE: PATH).The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software.

As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight.

The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%.
Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate.

These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities.

Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending.Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity:Accelerating Defense AI Spending: A projected $55.3 billion global AI aerospace and defense market by 2030 creates a substantial addressable environment for companies supplying mission intelligence and decision-support technology.Smarter Autonomous Drone Operations: AI-enabled mission planning and sensor fusion can help unmanned aircraft interpret incoming data, adapt to changing conditions and coordinate operations with less manual intervention.Real-Time Intelligence and Decision Support: Military organizations need to process information from drones, satellites, radar and ground sensors quickly.

AI systems that reduce information overload and improve situational awareness could become increasingly valuable.Growing Demand for Autonomous Defense Systems: The AI-powered autonomous defense system market is forecast to reach $34.02 billion by 2030, reflecting growing investment in automated detection, operational coordination and defensive capabilities.Long-Term Software and Integration Potential: Companies that develop adaptable AI platforms capable of operating across multiple unmanned systems and mission environments may have opportunities to pursue defense contracts, licensing agreements, system integration projects and recurring software revenue.

Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either.“Autonomy is ultimately an intelligence problem, not simply a vehicle problem,” said Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave.

Stratum AI is being developed as the intelligence and orchestration layer connecting that ecosystem.”Agentic AI Mission Orchestration - VisionWave is designing the architecture around three principal functions:Mission orchestration — coordinating autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows;Sensor fusion — combining field information into actionable decision support; andAutonomy orchestration — connecting defense, homeland-security and commercial autonomous assets through a common command environment.
The Company’s longer-term objective is a system designed around one operator, one operating picture and multiple autonomous domains.

Highlighting these achievements are the recent successful flight tests of the TDI-J85 (J85) engine across multiple configurations, including Lugged Launch, Palletized, and Surface-to-Surface applications.“Our successful flight tests across diverse deployment methods prove the versatility and reliability of the TDI-J85 engine,” said Joseph Kovasity, Senior Vice President of Kratos TDI.

The achievement demonstrates Ondas' capabilities in delivering complex, fully integrated protection systems that meet stringent international aviation certification requirements.AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV) and NIOA Australia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to explore opportunities to expand Australian industry participation supporting AV’s one-way attack systems.Signed during LAND FORCES 2026, the agreement establishes a framework for AV and NIOA to identify and facilitate a path forward for the localization, co-production and sustainment of AV’s one-way attack systems in Australia.Under the MOU, the companies will explore opportunities to combine AV’s autonomous systems with NIOA’s sovereign weapons and munitions expertise.

Potential areas of cooperation include local manufacturing and integration, in-country support and sustainment, and the development of Australian variants incorporating NIOA-developed payloads, warheads and mission effects where technically, commercially and legally feasible.UiPath, Inc. (NYSE: PATH), a leader in business orchestration and automation, recently announced it has been recognized as a Leader in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Agentic Software Quality Assurance Platforms.
