extraction.body: NEW YORK , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Platinum Trade Alerts (PTA) News Commentary - Advanced AI, real-time battlefield intelligence and autonomous coordination are reshaping the future of defense operations as global investment accelerates. - Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. The market is already attracting significant attention. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV ), BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), Palladyne AI Corp. (NASDAQ: PDYN ), AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: AIRO ), MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: MVIS ). The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software. As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight. The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%. Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate. These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities. Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending. Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity: VisionWave (NASDAQ: VWAV ) Advances Stratum AI, an Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Mission Intelligence and Orchestration - VisionWave Holdings Inc. ("VisionWave" or the "Company") today highlighted the development of Stratum AI, the Company's agentic artificial intelligence ("AI") mission-intelligence and orchestration layer, which is under development and is designed to connect autonomous platforms, sensors and mission workflows across defense, homeland security and commercial applications. Developing Intelligence Layer Is Designed to Coordinate Autonomous Systems, AI Agents, Sensor Fusion and Mission Workflows Across Air and Ground Stratum AI is being developed alongside STRATUM Command, a further AI-enabled sensing, mission-intelligence and situational-awareness capability that is likewise under development. Together, the technologies are intended to coordinate autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows while fusing field information and delivering real-time decision support. These capabilities are under development. Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either. Other recent developments in the autonomous, AI industries of note include: BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), a specialized security and defense technology company providing mission-ready AI, announced it has secured more than $225 million in contract awards since July across homeland security, defense, intelligence and federal civilian customers. The awards represent both new wins and successful recompetes in the core of BigBear.ai's business, which is focused on expanding in the National Security and Trade & Travel markets. "Retaining critical work with CBP while adding the FBI, the Coast Guard and new defense and intelligence customers is proof of a strong foundation and an expanding customer base," said Kevin McAleenan, CEO of BigBear.ai. "Technology does not translate into capability without operational insight, and these awards come from customers who understand both the depth of our experience and our differentiated technology." As part of these wins, BigBear.ai won more than 25 new generative AI awards across federal agencies, including the FBI, NASA, the U.S. Coast Guard, the Department of Energy and the Department of Veterans Affairs. Customer teams use BigBear.ai's generative AI platforms and products for secure access to the latest generative AI models and agentic tools, with the choice of available models from leading AI and cloud providers, and demand continues to grow across defense, intelligence and civilian agencies, including in disconnected and air-gapped environments. In addition to winning new customers in federal law enforcement with the FBI and domestic security with the U.S. Coast Guard, new contracts across the totality of the BigBear.ai business include combatant commands such as U.S. Central Command and U.S. Southern Command, and new classified awards supporting intelligence customers. Federal Ammunition, part of The Kinetic Group, a member of CSG Group; Mossberg; and Palladyne AI Corp. (NASDAQ: PDYN ), recently announced the joint development of SwarmShot™, a modular autonomous airborne counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) designed to transform compatible drones into reusable air-to-air interceptors operating together as a collaborative kinetic defensive swarm. SwarmShot will combine Federal's specialized counter-UAS shotshell ammunition, a lightweight Mossberg weapon module purpose-engineered for airborne operation, and Palladyne AI's IntelliSwarm™ autonomy system, which combines BRAIN avionics with SwarmOS™ collaborative autonomy software. The system will initially be developed as a modular mission add-on for Gremlin-X™, Palladyne AI's Group 1 quadcopter mini-bomber. The modular architecture is intended to allow the same aircraft to be configured for either its existing mini-bomber precision-strike mission or an autonomous counter-UAS mission. Following qualification on Gremlin-X, the companies plan to offer SwarmShot to other manufacturers as an integration kit for compatible unmanned aircraft. SwarmShot will be engineered as one integrated system. Federal will lead ammunition design and terminal-effect optimization, leveraging experience from its recent U.S. Army counter-UAS ammunition contract. Mossberg will lead development of the lightweight airborne weapon module, including remote operation, recoil management, reliability, and safety. Palladyne AI will lead UAS integration, fire control, terminal-intercept autonomy, and coordination among multiple interceptors. AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: AIRO ), a next-generation aerospace and defense company, recently announced that Jaunt Air Mobility has selected Calogy Solutions to design the battery system for its recently unveiled next-generation hybrid-electric, JC-250 and JX-250 VTOL drone variants. The collaboration marks another key milestone in Jaunt's development of advanced autonomous aircraft designed to support defense, commercial, and industrial missions. By integrating innovative battery engineering and thermal management technology, Jaunt continues to advance a platform engineered for safe, reliable, and high-performance operation in demanding environments. Calogy Solutions will develop the battery system using its proprietary Uni.T™ passive air-cooling technology, which delivers liquid-cooling performance without the weight and complexity of traditional liquid-cooled systems. The lightweight architecture is designed to support reliable operation across a wide range of environmental conditions while helping mitigate thermal runaway propagation to enhance overall system safety. "We are pleased to partner with Calogy Solutions as we advance the development of our next-generation hybrid-electric VTOL platform," said Eric Côté, President, Jaunt Air Mobility Canada. "Their expertise in battery engineering and their innovative thermal management technology align well with our focus on building a safe, reliable and high-performance aircraft capable of operating in demanding environments. We look forward to working together as we move the program toward flight testing and commercialization." MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: MVIS ) , a leader in advanced perception solutions for industrial, security and defense, and automotive applications, and Robinson Unmanned have entered into a joint marketing and demonstration agreement to advance integration of MicroVision's MOVIA™ Air Plus lidar technology with Robinson Unmanned's SPIRIT™ Group 1 unmanned aircraft system (UAS) for real-time mapping applications. The companies are collaborating to demonstrate how compact airborne lidar can capture, process, and generate detailed spatial information in real time, helping reduce the time between data collection and actionable insight. The integrated capability has potential applications across commercial, civil, public safety and global defense markets where rapidly changing conditions can make timely situational awareness and actionable data critical. "Robinson Unmanned brings deep expertise in UAS platforms and understands what customers need from airborne systems operating in demanding environments," said Glen DeVos, Chief Executive Officer of MicroVision. "Integrating MOVIA Air Plus with their platform demonstrates how our lidar technology can enable real-time mapping and situational awareness from the air. We see significant opportunities to apply these capabilities across commercial, civil, security, and defense markets." Mossberg will lead development of the lightweight airborne weapon module, including remote operation, recoil management, reliability, and safety. Palladyne AI will lead UAS integration, fire control, terminal-intercept autonomy, and coordination among multiple interceptors.

AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: AIRO ), a next-generation aerospace and defense company, recently announced that Jaunt Air Mobility has selected Calogy Solutions to design the battery system for its recently unveiled next-generation hybrid-electric, JC-250 and JX-250 VTOL drone variants.

The collaboration marks another key milestone in Jaunt's development of advanced autonomous aircraft designed to support defense, commercial, and industrial missions. By integrating innovative battery engineering and thermal management technology, Jaunt continues to advance a platform engineered for safe, reliable, and high-performance operation in demanding environments.

(NASDAQ: MVIS ) , a leader in advanced perception solutions for industrial, security and defense, and automotive applications, and Robinson Unmanned have entered into a joint marketing and demonstration agreement to advance integration of MicroVision's MOVIA™ Air Plus lidar technology with Robinson Unmanned's SPIRIT™ Group 1 unmanned aircraft system (UAS) for real-time mapping applications.

The companies are collaborating to demonstrate how compact airborne lidar can capture, process, and generate detailed spatial information in real time, helping reduce the time between data collection and actionable insight. The integrated capability has potential applications across commercial, civil, public safety and global defense markets where rapidly changing conditions can make timely situational awareness and actionable data critical.

"Integrating MOVIA Air Plus with their platform demonstrates how our lidar technology can enable real-time mapping and situational awareness from the air. D-FLY™ - Autonomous Counter-UAS Intercept Platform - D-FLY™ is a rapid-response autonomous aerial interceptor designed specifically to address the growing global threat posed by hostile drones and low-altitude unmanned aerial systems. (NASDAQ: ONDS ), a leading provider of autonomous drone and advanced defense technologies, announced that it has secured more than $40 million in aggregate new orders during June for autonomous defense systems, including Counter-UAS ("C-UAS") solutions, Loitering Munition Systems ("LMS"), ground systems and related defense services from governmental and defense customers across multiple international markets. extraction.body: Billions in Defense Modernization Are Driving Demand for Advanced AI, Autonomous Coordination, and Next-Generation Battlefield IntelligenceNEW YORK, Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV), Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ: ONDS), AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV), UiPath, Inc. (NYSE: PATH).The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software. As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight. The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%. Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate. These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities. Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending.Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity:Accelerating Defense AI Spending: A projected $55.3 billion global AI aerospace and defense market by 2030 creates a substantial addressable environment for companies supplying mission intelligence and decision-support technology.Smarter Autonomous Drone Operations: AI-enabled mission planning and sensor fusion can help unmanned aircraft interpret incoming data, adapt to changing conditions and coordinate operations with less manual intervention.Real-Time Intelligence and Decision Support: Military organizations need to process information from drones, satellites, radar and ground sensors quickly. AI systems that reduce information overload and improve situational awareness could become increasingly valuable.Growing Demand for Autonomous Defense Systems: The AI-powered autonomous defense system market is forecast to reach $34.02 billion by 2030, reflecting growing investment in automated detection, operational coordination and defensive capabilities.Long-Term Software and Integration Potential: Companies that develop adaptable AI platforms capable of operating across multiple unmanned systems and mission environments may have opportunities to pursue defense contracts, licensing agreements, system integration projects and recurring software revenue. Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either.“Autonomy is ultimately an intelligence problem, not simply a vehicle problem,” said Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave. Stratum AI is being developed as the intelligence and orchestration layer connecting that ecosystem.”Agentic AI Mission Orchestration - VisionWave is designing the architecture around three principal functions:Mission orchestration — coordinating autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows;Sensor fusion — combining field information into actionable decision support; andAutonomy orchestration — connecting defense, homeland-security and commercial autonomous assets through a common command environment. The Company’s longer-term objective is a system designed around one operator, one operating picture and multiple autonomous domains. Highlighting these achievements are the recent successful flight tests of the TDI-J85 (J85) engine across multiple configurations, including Lugged Launch, Palletized, and Surface-to-Surface applications.“Our successful flight tests across diverse deployment methods prove the versatility and reliability of the TDI-J85 engine,” said Joseph Kovasity, Senior Vice President of Kratos TDI. The achievement demonstrates Ondas' capabilities in delivering complex, fully integrated protection systems that meet stringent international aviation certification requirements.AeroVironment, Inc. Potential areas of cooperation include local manufacturing and integration, in-country support and sustainment, and the development of Australian variants incorporating NIOA-developed payloads, warheads and mission effects where technically, commercially and legally feasible.UiPath, Inc. extraction.body: NEW YORK , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Platinum Trade Alerts (PTA) News Commentary - Advanced AI, real-time battlefield intelligence and autonomous coordination are reshaping the future of defense operations as global investment accelerates. - Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. The market is already attracting significant attention. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV ), BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), Palladyne AI Corp. (NASDAQ: PDYN ), AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: AIRO ), MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: MVIS ). The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software. As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight. The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%. Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate. These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities. Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending. Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity: VisionWave (NASDAQ: VWAV ) Advances Stratum AI, an Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Mission Intelligence and Orchestration - VisionWave Holdings Inc. ("VisionWave" or the "Company") today highlighted the development of Stratum AI, the Company's agentic artificial intelligence ("AI") mission-intelligence and orchestration layer, which is under development and is designed to connect autonomous platforms, sensors and mission workflows across defense, homeland security and commercial applications. Developing Intelligence Layer Is Designed to Coordinate Autonomous Systems, AI Agents, Sensor Fusion and Mission Workflows Across Air and Ground Stratum AI is being developed alongside STRATUM Command, a further AI-enabled sensing, mission-intelligence and situational-awareness capability that is likewise under development. Together, the technologies are intended to coordinate autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows while fusing field information and delivering real-time decision support. These capabilities are under development. Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either. Other recent developments in the autonomous, AI industries of note include: BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), a specialized security and defense technology company providing mission-ready AI, announced it has secured more than $225 million in contract awards since July across homeland security, defense, intelligence and federal civilian customers. The awards represent both new wins and successful recompetes in the core of BigBear.ai's business, which is focused on expanding in the National Security and Trade & Travel markets. "Retaining critical work with CBP while adding the FBI, the Coast Guard and new defense and intelligence customers is proof of a strong foundation and an expanding customer base," said Kevin McAleenan, CEO of BigBear.ai. "Technology does not translate into capability without operational insight, and these awards come from customers who understand both the depth of our experience and our differentiated technology." As part of these wins, BigBear.ai won more than 25 new generative AI awards across federal agencies, including the FBI, NASA, the U.S. Coast Guard, the Department of Energy and the Department of Veterans Affairs. Customer teams use BigBear.ai's generative AI platforms and products for secure access to the latest generative AI models and agentic tools, with the choice of available models from leading AI and cloud providers, and demand continues to grow across defense, intelligence and civilian agencies, including in disconnected and air-gapped environments. In addition to winning new customers in federal law enforcement with the FBI and domestic security with the U.S. Coast Guard, new contracts across the totality of the BigBear.ai business include combatant commands such as U.S. Central Command and U.S. Southern Command, and new classified awards supporting intelligence customers. Federal Ammunition, part of The Kinetic Group, a member of CSG Group; Mossberg; and Palladyne AI Corp. (NASDAQ: PDYN ), recently announced the joint development of SwarmShot™, a modular autonomous airborne counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) designed to transform compatible drones into reusable air-to-air interceptors operating together as a collaborative kinetic defensive swarm. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. The market is already attracting significant attention. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. sources.title: HomeView doesn’t natively support any video apps yet — not even Apple’s
passages: Apple says HomeView is “the perfect way” to enjoy its audio and video entertainment apps, but some notable examples like Apple TV only work if you AirPlay it through your iPhone.

As noted on the HomeView spec page, Apple TV, Apple Books audiobooks, Apple Music Classical, and Apple News Plus aren’t natively supported on the smart hub, so you’ll have to use your phone to operate them.

The HomeView also doesn’t have an App Store (which is typical for smart home hubs), which makes that CarPlay connection even more significant for third-party app developers, since apps that support projecting video or audio through the platform will work easily from day one.

HomeView is foremostly designed as a hub for managing smart home gadgets, but competing smart display hardware like Amazon’s Echo Show and Google’s Nest Hub devices can natively stream Prime Video and YouTube, respectively, without requiring a phone connection.

Apple TV is also featured in at least one promotional image for HomeView, but the AirPlay requirement is in small print on its announcement page: > “Subscription may be required to access some content and services.

AARP had forecast a 3.5% increase a month ago.Other groups are forecasting a slightly lower COLA, with the Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group for older Americans, projecting a 3.5% adjustment, down from its prior estimate of 3.6%.A benefit increase of 3.6% would represent the biggest annual adjustment in Social Security payments since 2023.

extraction.body: Stubbornly hot inflation in August could push up the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment for Social Security recipients, according to a new estimate from AARP. The 2027 COLA is now projected at 3.6%, based on the August Consumer Price Index figures released on Wednesday, according to the advocacy group. AARP had forecast a 3.5% increase a month ago.Other groups are forecasting a slightly lower COLA, with the Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group for older Americans, projecting a 3.5% adjustment, down from its prior estimate of 3.6%.A benefit increase of 3.6% would represent the biggest annual adjustment in Social Security payments since 2023. The program's more than 70 million recipients rely on the annual cost-of-living adjustment to ensure their benefits keep up with inflation, although some critics say the measure has failed to offset the price pressures facing older Americans and people with disabilities, including rising healthcare costs."No matter if the COLA announcement comes in slightly higher or slightly lower than our prediction, seniors will probably end up disappointed in the long run," said Shannon Benton, executive director of the Senior Citizens League, in a statement. "The reality is that older Americans allocate their budgets differently than people still in the workforce, so inflation hits them differently."The average retired worker received $2,071 a month in Social Security benefits as of January, according to the Social Security Administration. That means a 3.6% COLA would increase the average monthly benefit by about $75, raising it to roughly $2,146 a month at the start of 2027. When will the official COLA be announced?The official COLA won't be announced until next month, when the Social Security Administration will calculate next year's inflation adjustment based on the July, August and September inflation data. The September CPI report will be released on Oct. 14, with the Social Security Administration set to announce the 2027 COLA the same day.Inflation remained elevated in August, with consumer prices rising 3.4% from a year ago. Economists are concerned that the rise in diesel, which powers the trucks and railroads that transport goods around the U.S., could trickle through the economy as businesses hike prices to offset their higher energy costs.Seniors, in the meantime, can feel that their COLA isn't keeping up with current inflation, experts say. For instance, the 2026 COLA, which went into effect in January's benefit payments, was set at 2.8%. "The COLA only happening once a year puts life on hold for a lot of seniors. When prices rise, they don't rise next January when your benefit check goes up," Benton said.

Baltimore, MD - The Social Security Administration (SSA) today announced a 3.6 percent benefit increase for 2027. Social Security benefits include Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI), and Supplemental Security Income (SSI). On average, Social Security retirement benefits will increase by $75 per month. Nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will see a 3.6 percent cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) beginning in January 2027. Increased payments to about 7.3 million people receiving SSI will begin on December 31, 2026. (Note: Some people receive both Social Security benefits and SSI). “Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” said Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano . “Under President Donald J. Trump, Social Security is delivering better, faster, higher-quality service for the American people." Individuals with personal my Social Security accounts can view their COLA notice online starting in late November—up to three weeks earlier than receiving a paper notice in the mail. Account holders can also choose to receive text or email alerts when a new message, including their COLA notice, is available in their personal my Social Security account’s Message Center. Individuals who do not have a personal account will need to create one and enroll in paperless notices by November 18 to see their COLA notice online. Create an account today at www.ssa.gov/myaccount . Individuals who have not enrolled in paperless notices in my Social Security will receive their COLA notice by mail in December. Social Security beneficiaries will receive a simplified, one-page COLA notice, which uses plain and personalized language, and provides exact dates and dollar amounts of an individual’s new benefit amount and any deductions. Information about Medicare changes for 2027 will be available at www.medicare.gov . For Medicare enrollees, the 2027 premium amount will be available via my Social Security Message Center starting in late November. Individuals who have not opted to receive messages online will receive their COLA notice by mail in December. The Social Security Act provides for how the COLA is calculated. The Social Security Act ties the annual COLA to the increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) as determined by the Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics. For additional information, visit www.ssa.gov/cola . NOTE TO CORRESPONDENTS: Here is the COLA 2027 Fact Sheet showing an easy-to-understand overview of all the various automatic adjustments for 2027. For more information about Social Security’s services, visit www.ssa.gov . For more Social Security news, follow the agency on X @SocialSecurity .

Bisignano . “Under President Donald J. Trump, Social Security is delivering better, faster, higher-quality service for the American people." Individuals with personal my Social Security accounts can view their COLA notice online starting in late November—up to three weeks earlier than receiving a paper notice in the mail. Attendees saw a Hong victory as a path to take back the governor’s office, where Democratic Gov. Tony Evers has blocked conservative bills for nearly eight years. In recent weeks, Tiffany and fellow Republicans attacked Hong over past social media posts, including calls to abolish the U.S. Senate, defund police and cancel Thanksgiving. They saw the posts as signs Hong would be a weak general election opponent. “We’re hoping that Hong will win the primaries because what she says is just outright insanity,” 19-year-old Tiffany campaign worker Ellie Guida said. Instead, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley eked out a comeback victory to win the Democratic nomination. And now a new poll shows why Republicans have reason to worry. Crowley led Tiffany 48% to 44% in a new Badger Battleground Poll conducted Aug. 12 and 13 by Platform Communications. Crowley also led 42% to 30% among independents and 54% to 35% in competitive Assembly districts. Tiffany was viewed unfavorably by 43% of poll respondents, compared with 26% with an unfavorable view of Crowley, with 31% lacking a solid opinion of Crowley. The margin of error was 4.4 percentage points, and the poll was conducted via landline and cellphone interviews. Still, even attendees at Crowley’s watch party in Milwaukee raised concerns about whether he can persuade Hong voters to support him in the general election. Keith Schmitz, leader of the suburban Milwaukee progressive group Grassroots North Shore, said Hong’s supporters are more likely to back Crowley if Hong strongly endorses him. Tiffany began a “Common-Sense Leadership Tour” in Green Bay Wednesday with Republican lieutenant governor nominee David Varnam and Attorney General nominee Eric Toney. Brandon Scholz, former chair of the Republican Party of Wisconsin and now an independent political analyst, highlighted how facing Crowley instead of Hong changes the challenge for Tiffany. He pointed to Crowley being “more measured in his responses and comments,” along with his more moderate positions. “It will be hard, I think, for Tiffany to do the damage to Crowley that he could have done to Hong,” Scholz said. Tiffany claimed there was no difference between Crowley and “a socialist.” The ad highlighted Milwaukee County budget deficits under Crowley and suggested that portended mismanagement, higher prices and increased taxes if he became governor. In response, a Crowley spokesperson said Tiffany was in “meltdown mode” as he prepared to face Crowley. The spokesperson called the attack “a desperate effort to distract from his own extreme record of voting 100% of the time to advance Donald Trump’s extreme MAGA agenda.” The statement said Crowley lowered property taxes and created new jobs, and criticized Tiffany’s support for Trump’s tariffs and his missed votes on a bipartisan bill aiming to lower housing costs . Many people don’t tune in to primaries until a few weeks before voting, Franklin added. He pointed to Evers’ endorsement late in the race. Martin’s lieutenant governor campaign website focused largely on developing energy resources and protecting public safety. sources.title: As data centers remain potent political issue, David Crowley offers plan to regulate artificial intelligence in Wisconsin
passages: In a governor’s race that has focused more on data center construction than artificial intelligence technology, Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley on Tuesday announced a plan for state regulations on AI aimed at protecting vulnerable Wisconsinites.
In an 11-point plan shared with Wisconsin Watch, Crowley calls for guardrails on AI offerings for minors and holding technology companies responsible for scams and fraud on their platforms.

Additionally, Attorney General Josh Kaul in August announced Wisconsin could receive up to $313 million in a settlement social media company Meta made with 47 states in a case that alleged addictive components of its platforms threatened teens’ mental health.

In a statement, Tiffany also said Wisconsin needs “commonsense guardrails” to protect children and older adults, including holding companies accountable for platforms that allow creation of sexually explicit images or engage minors in inappropriate chatbot conversations.
Tiffany, and the rest of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation, voted for the bill in 2025.

“Like so many parents, Ericka and I are raising our three girls in the age of social media and AI, and we’re navigating things no generation before us has ever had to, worrying about whether a stranger is messaging our kids, or a fake picture of our daughter is going around school, or even scammers trying to drain a grandparent’s life savings,” Crowley said.
The proposals in Crowley’s regulatory plan would require state legislative action.

extraction.body: In a governor’s race that has focused more on data center construction than artificial intelligence technology, Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley on Tuesday announced a plan for state regulations on AI aimed at protecting vulnerable Wisconsinites. In an 11-point plan shared with Wisconsin Watch, Crowley calls for guardrails on AI offerings for minors and holding technology companies responsible for scams and fraud on their platforms. Some key components of the plan include: Limiting access to AI chatbot apps for children under 13. Prohibiting addictive design features, such as infinite scrolling and autoplay, on accounts of minors. Increasing penalties for circulating AI-generated sexual images of minors. Allowing families to sue AI platforms if their content harms children, such as by promoting suicide or eating disorders. More funding for adult protective services and resource centers that can help victims of scams or fraud. Crowley, the Milwaukee county executive, is running for governor against Republican U.S. Tom Tiffany in what polling from Marquette University Law School shows could be another close governor’s race in Wisconsin. AI policy debates between the two candidates in the months since the August primary have mostly been focused on the planning and construction of AI data centers, rather than the technology itself. In a statement, Tiffany also said Wisconsin needs “commonsense guardrails” to protect children and older adults, including holding companies accountable for platforms that allow creation of sexually explicit images or engage minors in inappropriate chatbot conversations. Tiffany said he also wants to prevent personal data from “falling into the hands of foreign adversaries, including Communist China.” “As governor, I will also support commonsense age-verification requirements for app providers, strengthen parental-consent protections, and give parents greater control over their children’s online activity,” Tiffany said. Crowley’s proposed state-level AI regulations land as President Donald Trump has dismissed calls for guardrails and warnings from technology company leaders asking for government oversight as their platforms become more advanced. Trump in May 2025 signed the Take it Down Act, which criminalized the online publication of real and AI-generated intimate images and requires social media platforms to remove them once notified of their existence. Tiffany, and the rest of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation, voted for the bill in 2025. Other proposed federal legislation has not advanced, including bills requiring public reporting of safety incidents by AI companies and requiring labels on any AI-generated content. Crowley in a statement said he would not “wait around for DC to act” on additional AI regulations if he is elected. “Like so many parents, Ericka and I are raising our three girls in the age of social media and AI, and we’re navigating things no generation before us has ever had to, worrying about whether a stranger is messaging our kids, or a fake picture of our daughter is going around school, or even scammers trying to drain a grandparent’s life savings,” Crowley said. The proposals in Crowley’s regulatory plan would require state legislative action. Additionally, Attorney General Josh Kaul in August announced Wisconsin could receive up to $313 million in a settlement social media company Meta made with 47 states in a case that alleged addictive components of its platforms threatened teens’ mental health.

They saw the posts as signs Hong would be a weak general election opponent. “We’re hoping that Hong will win the primaries because what she says is just outright insanity,” 19-year-old Tiffany campaign worker Ellie Guida said. Crowley also led 42% to 30% among independents and 54% to 35% in competitive Assembly districts. Tiffany was viewed unfavorably by 43% of poll respondents, compared with 26% with an unfavorable view of Crowley, with 31% lacking a solid opinion of Crowley. The margin of error was 4.4 percentage points, and the poll was conducted via landline and cellphone interviews. Still, even attendees at Crowley’s watch party in Milwaukee raised concerns about whether he can persuade Hong voters to support him in the general election. Tiffany claimed there was no difference between Crowley and “a socialist.” The ad highlighted Milwaukee County budget deficits under Crowley and suggested that portended mismanagement, higher prices and increased taxes if he became governor. In response, a Crowley spokesperson said Tiffany was in “meltdown mode” as he prepared to face Crowley. The spokesperson called the attack “a desperate effort to distract from his own extreme record of voting 100% of the time to advance Donald Trump’s extreme MAGA agenda.” The statement said Crowley lowered property taxes and created new jobs, and criticized Tiffany’s support for Trump’s tariffs and his missed votes on a bipartisan bill aiming to lower housing costs . Many people don’t tune in to primaries until a few weeks before voting, Franklin added. He pointed to Evers’ endorsement late in the race. sources.title: As data centers remain potent political issue, David Crowley offers plan to regulate artificial intelligence in Wisconsin
passages: In a governor’s race that has focused more on data center construction than artificial intelligence technology, Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley on Tuesday announced a plan for state regulations on AI aimed at protecting vulnerable Wisconsinites.
In an 11-point plan shared with Wisconsin Watch, Crowley calls for guardrails on AI offerings for minors and holding technology companies responsible for scams and fraud on their platforms.

Additionally, Attorney General Josh Kaul in August announced Wisconsin could receive up to $313 million in a settlement social media company Meta made with 47 states in a case that alleged addictive components of its platforms threatened teens’ mental health.

In a statement, Tiffany also said Wisconsin needs “commonsense guardrails” to protect children and older adults, including holding companies accountable for platforms that allow creation of sexually explicit images or engage minors in inappropriate chatbot conversations.
Tiffany, and the rest of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation, voted for the bill in 2025.

“Like so many parents, Ericka and I are raising our three girls in the age of social media and AI, and we’re navigating things no generation before us has ever had to, worrying about whether a stranger is messaging our kids, or a fake picture of our daughter is going around school, or even scammers trying to drain a grandparent’s life savings,” Crowley said.
The proposals in Crowley’s regulatory plan would require state legislative action.

extraction.body: In a governor’s race that has focused more on data center construction than artificial intelligence technology, Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley on Tuesday announced a plan for state regulations on AI aimed at protecting vulnerable Wisconsinites. In an 11-point plan shared with Wisconsin Watch, Crowley calls for guardrails on AI offerings for minors and holding technology companies responsible for scams and fraud on their platforms. Some key components of the plan include: Limiting access to AI chatbot apps for children under 13. Prohibiting addictive design features, such as infinite scrolling and autoplay, on accounts of minors. Increasing penalties for circulating AI-generated sexual images of minors. Allowing families to sue AI platforms if their content harms children, such as by promoting suicide or eating disorders. More funding for adult protective services and resource centers that can help victims of scams or fraud. Crowley, the Milwaukee county executive, is running for governor against Republican U.S. Tom Tiffany in what polling from Marquette University Law School shows could be another close governor’s race in Wisconsin. AI policy debates between the two candidates in the months since the August primary have mostly been focused on the planning and construction of AI data centers, rather than the technology itself. In a statement, Tiffany also said Wisconsin needs “commonsense guardrails” to protect children and older adults, including holding companies accountable for platforms that allow creation of sexually explicit images or engage minors in inappropriate chatbot conversations. Tiffany said he also wants to prevent personal data from “falling into the hands of foreign adversaries, including Communist China.” “As governor, I will also support commonsense age-verification requirements for app providers, strengthen parental-consent protections, and give parents greater control over their children’s online activity,” Tiffany said. Crowley’s proposed state-level AI regulations land as President Donald Trump has dismissed calls for guardrails and warnings from technology company leaders asking for government oversight as their platforms become more advanced. Trump in May 2025 signed the Take it Down Act, which criminalized the online publication of real and AI-generated intimate images and requires social media platforms to remove them once notified of their existence. Tiffany, and the rest of Wisconsin’s congressional delegation, voted for the bill in 2025. Other proposed federal legislation has not advanced, including bills requiring public reporting of safety incidents by AI companies and requiring labels on any AI-generated content. Crowley in a statement said he would not “wait around for DC to act” on additional AI regulations if he is elected. “Like so many parents, Ericka and I are raising our three girls in the age of social media and AI, and we’re navigating things no generation before us has ever had to, worrying about whether a stranger is messaging our kids, or a fake picture of our daughter is going around school, or even scammers trying to drain a grandparent’s life savings,” Crowley said. The proposals in Crowley’s regulatory plan would require state legislative action. Additionally, Attorney General Josh Kaul in August announced Wisconsin could receive up to $313 million in a settlement social media company Meta made with 47 states in a case that alleged addictive components of its platforms threatened teens’ mental health.

extraction.body: U.S. inflation sped up more than expected in September, perhaps putting multiple Federal Reserve rate hikes back into play. The September Consumer Price Index rose 0.6%, according to a Wednesday morning report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That’s up from 0.4% in August, and in line with economist forecasts for 0.6%. On a year-over-year basis, however, CPI rose 3.7% versus 3.4% in August and above estimates for 3.6%. Core CPI — which strips out food and energy costs — also disappointed, rising 0.3% in September. That was the same pace as August, but above consensus forecasts for 0.2%. Year-over-year core CPI was higher by 2.6% versus 2.4% the previous month and above estimates for 2.5%. Bitcoin BTC $83,212.45 dropped $1,000 on the news, now trading at $82,800. The 10-year Treasury yield has shot higher by 6.5 basis points to 5.284%. U.S. stock index futures are all lower, the Nasdaq 100 leading with a 0.65% decline. Ahead of the data, a string of Fed speakers had hinted that the central bank was likely to raise interest rates another 25 basis points before year-end. Market pricing reflected that information, with most expecting the central bank to pause at its upcoming meeting later this month, but hike at its final meeting of the year in early December.

"She ended up having a second breast cancer in her other breast that would have gone undetected if it weren’t for contrast enhanced mammogram," Pearce said.
The women who are high-risk for breast cancer are guided to alternate each year between a mammogram and an MRI.
According to Mercy Hospital Oklahoma City, the intravenous contrast dye collects in the blood vessels of abnormal tissues, enabling a breast radiologist to study those areas in more detail.

extraction.body: A woman in Oklahoma knew she had breast cancer but a new technology at a local hospital detected something else she didn't expect. According to Mercy Hospital Oklahoma City, the intravenous contrast dye collects in the blood vessels of abnormal tissues, enabling a breast radiologist to study those areas in more detail. "If it’s something abnormal, it will light up with the contrast and it takes away the rest of that dense breast tissue that might have covered it up on a traditional mammogram," said Dr. Melanie Pearce, director of breast imaging at Mercy Hospital. The specific machine at Mercy Hospital is the GE Pristina Serena that can take 2D and 3D images, conduct biopsies and uses the CESM to help patients quicker. "It’s faster, it’s more comfortable, it’s less expensive also," said Pearce. Pearce learned about the technology years ago, but now her patients are benefitting from it. The fact that the very first patient that had the exam had an important finding with an outcome that would affect her care, at this level, I can’t even find the words," Pearce said. The first woman to get scanned with the machine knew she had cancer in one breast but when the staff at Mercy used the new technology, a mass was detected in her other breast. It’s a life changer for patients," Pearce said. The unnamed patient's story shows how the machine can affect the health of women who get tested. "She ended up having a second breast cancer in her other breast that would have gone undetected if it weren’t for contrast enhanced mammogram," Pearce said. Breast cancer is the second leading cancer in the U.S. for women and affects more than 240,000 women every year. Women are advised to start getting mammograms at 40, and even younger if a woman is determined to be high-risk for the disease. The women who are high-risk for breast cancer are guided to alternate each year between a mammogram and an MRI. Pearce said the new technology at Mercy is as effective as an MRI to detect cancers–plus it's cheaper. "Certain types of imaging tests can be very expensive," she said. "And with the contrast enhanced mammogram, it’s the cost of a diagnostic mammogram plus the contrast that you get." Pearce said early detection can translate to better care outcomes and decisions, better communication between patients and their medical teams, and better quality of care. Pearce said the test is more comfortable for woman, as they can sit instead of laying down. The wait times between answers is also lower as the new technology has so many capabilities. "We can just take care of it on the same machine that we see it on," Pearce said.

passages: The thought of receiving a positive test result understandably makes women nervous, but as Brem notes, "We don't get rid of the disease by not knowing we have it."Early detection of breast cancer leads to significantly better outcomes compared to cases where breast cancer is found in its later stages.

The software can also predict future risk of breast cancer even when none is detected in a mammogram."Imagine what the impact of that is going to be on survival therapy," Brem said.If women begin getting screened at age 35 with AI-enhanced readings, she noted the software will constantly teach itself how to improve in detecting breast cancer with each analysis.

Brem wants to change this with her foundation, which for the past 20 years has championed early detection through innovative screening, increased education and awareness, and equitable access."I look forward to the more wide-reaching implementation of AI to help not only find more cancers, but with healthcare," she said.A breast cancer breath test?Brem is helping to develop a breath test that could detect breast cancer.

For those under 40 who think they have time until they need to start screening for breast cancer, think again."You're not too young to have breast cancer," Brem warns.Having the conversation now about your plan for breast cancer screenings and seeking out additional exams is essential in early detection and better prognosis.

Often, the AI readings cost extra, which may make the option inaccessible for some."There is nothing you can do to absolutely prevent breast cancer," Brem acknowledged.But she said, "One of the things AI can do is really equalize the inequalities," referring to the racial disparities that affect diagnosis and treatment for many women."Black women die at a 40% higher rate [from breast cancer] than White women," Brem noted, and women with fewer resources have less access to mammograms.
And there's hope it could someday help beyond breast cancer.

extraction.body: Rachel Brem decided at age 12 that she wanted to cure cancer after her mom was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was early detection that led to her mother living way past her prognosis of six months. Now, Brem is working to improve breast cancer screening for all women.Brem is a board-certified diagnostic radiologist and director of Breast Imaging and Intervention at George Washington University. She created the Brem Foundation to help prevent breast cancer from taking more lives. On this week's episode of "Healthful," she discussed the innovation that makes her hopeful.Artificial intelligence and breast imaging"AI is going to change everything in medicine, and certainly breast cancer detection," Brem said.In addition to her work with George Washington University's Breast Imaging and Intervention unit, Brem collaborates with ScreenPoint Medical to develop Transpara, an AI breast cancer screening software.Already there is significant scientific research showing mammograms paired with AI evaluations "can find cancer up to five years earlier," she said, by detecting warning signs in women that might be missed with just mammograms alone. The software can also predict future risk of breast cancer even when none is detected in a mammogram."Imagine what the impact of that is going to be on survival therapy," Brem said.If women begin getting screened at age 35 with AI-enhanced readings, she noted the software will constantly teach itself how to improve in detecting breast cancer with each analysis. That's younger than the starting age recommended by several major medical organizations.At George Washington University, Brem said, "we've been using AI for over four years in every mammogram," adding that using the software does not cost extra.However, nationwide, just 20% of practices use AI with their mammogram procedures. Often, the AI readings cost extra, which may make the option inaccessible for some."There is nothing you can do to absolutely prevent breast cancer," Brem acknowledged.But she said, "One of the things AI can do is really equalize the inequalities," referring to the racial disparities that affect diagnosis and treatment for many women."Black women die at a 40% higher rate [from breast cancer] than White women," Brem noted, and women with fewer resources have less access to mammograms. Brem wants to change this with her foundation, which for the past 20 years has championed early detection through innovative screening, increased education and awareness, and equitable access."I look forward to the more wide-reaching implementation of AI to help not only find more cancers, but with healthcare," she said.A breast cancer breath test?Brem is helping to develop a breath test that could detect breast cancer. "It's not available yet, but I'm really excited about having no pain, no compression, and no injection way of diagnosing if you're accurately diagnosed," Brem said. And there's hope it could someday help beyond breast cancer. "The next step on our roadmap is not just breast cancer but a women's health panel where you could do one breath and get all these tests done," Brem said. The current state of breast cancer screeningThe guidelines from the American College of Physicians stated in 2026 that women over the age of 50 should get a mammogram every other year. The United States Preventive Services Task Force recommends that women should start screening every other year at the age of 40. To Brem, "This is a travesty.""Women will die if they listen to that."From her research, women should get checked for breast cancer annually starting at the age of 40. For those with a history of breast cancer in their family, they should start at 35.This is all easier said than done. Women often cite anxiety as a reason they delay or skip getting screened. The thought of receiving a positive test result understandably makes women nervous, but as Brem notes, "We don't get rid of the disease by not knowing we have it."Early detection of breast cancer leads to significantly better outcomes compared to cases where breast cancer is found in its later stages. "Ninety-nine percent of women with early breast cancer survive and thrive," Brem said, but this outcome can only be possible if women screen for it early and regularly.In addition to the recommended mammograms, Brem also believes "you absolutely, unequivocally definitely need more exams" if you have dense breasts. Half of women have dense breasts, and mammograms might not be able to pick up potentially deadly tumors hiding behind the tissue. Ultrasounds, MRIs or contrast-enhanced mammograms are necessary for those with dense breasts to get a complete view of their risks.Supplemental screening isn't always standard with some doctors. Brem advised that it is "really important" for women to insist that their doctors order these extra exams. The mammograms are not enough.Demand more, get educated, and "be badass"Brem is adamant in her belief that women can be proactive now to better their health and improve their breast cancer outcomes. For those under 40 who think they have time until they need to start screening for breast cancer, think again."You're not too young to have breast cancer," Brem warns.Having the conversation now about your plan for breast cancer screenings and seeking out additional exams is essential in early detection and better prognosis. "If you find it early, even if you're young, it's curable," Brem said.Rates of cancer are rising in younger women and awareness is the first step to being proactive about your health. Her foundation provides resources to educate women. Brem urges you to advocate for yourself at the doctor's office."We tell women to be badass," she said. It's what you deserve, and it's not a maybe."

The specific machine at Mercy Hospital is the GE Pristina Serena that can take 2D and 3D images, conduct biopsies and uses the CESM to help patients quicker. "It’s faster, it’s more comfortable, it’s less expensive also," said Pearce. Pearce learned about the technology years ago, but now her patients are benefitting from it. The fact that the very first patient that had the exam had an important finding with an outcome that would affect her care, at this level, I can’t even find the words," Pearce said. The first woman to get scanned with the machine knew she had cancer in one breast but when the staff at Mercy used the new technology, a mass was detected in her other breast. It’s a life changer for patients," Pearce said. The unnamed patient's story shows how the machine can affect the health of women who get tested. "She ended up having a second breast cancer in her other breast that would have gone undetected if it weren’t for contrast enhanced mammogram," Pearce said. Breast cancer is the second leading cancer in the U.S. for women and affects more than 240,000 women every year. Women are advised to start getting mammograms at 40, and even younger if a woman is determined to be high-risk for the disease. The women who are high-risk for breast cancer are guided to alternate each year between a mammogram and an MRI. Pearce said the new technology at Mercy is as effective as an MRI to detect cancers–plus it's cheaper. "Certain types of imaging tests can be very expensive," she said. "And with the contrast enhanced mammogram, it’s the cost of a diagnostic mammogram plus the contrast that you get." Pearce said early detection can translate to better care outcomes and decisions, better communication between patients and their medical teams, and better quality of care. Pearce said the test is more comfortable for woman, as they can sit instead of laying down. The wait times between answers is also lower as the new technology has so many capabilities. "We can just take care of it on the same machine that we see it on," Pearce said.

extraction.body: Rachel Brem decided at age 12 that she wanted to cure cancer after her mom was diagnosed with breast cancer. It was early detection that led to her mother living way past her prognosis of six months. Now, Brem is working to improve breast cancer screening for all women.Brem is a board-certified diagnostic radiologist and director of Breast Imaging and Intervention at George Washington University. She created the Brem Foundation to help prevent breast cancer from taking more lives. On this week's episode of "Healthful," she discussed the innovation that makes her hopeful.Artificial intelligence and breast imaging"AI is going to change everything in medicine, and certainly breast cancer detection," Brem said.In addition to her work with George Washington University's Breast Imaging and Intervention unit, Brem collaborates with ScreenPoint Medical to develop Transpara, an AI breast cancer screening software.Already there is significant scientific research showing mammograms paired with AI evaluations "can find cancer up to five years earlier," she said, by detecting warning signs in women that might be missed with just mammograms alone. The software can also predict future risk of breast cancer even when none is detected in a mammogram."Imagine what the impact of that is going to be on survival therapy," Brem said.If women begin getting screened at age 35 with AI-enhanced readings, she noted the software will constantly teach itself how to improve in detecting breast cancer with each analysis. That's younger than the starting age recommended by several major medical organizations.At George Washington University, Brem said, "we've been using AI for over four years in every mammogram," adding that using the software does not cost extra.However, nationwide, just 20% of practices use AI with their mammogram procedures. Often, the AI readings cost extra, which may make the option inaccessible for some."There is nothing you can do to absolutely prevent breast cancer," Brem acknowledged.But she said, "One of the things AI can do is really equalize the inequalities," referring to the racial disparities that affect diagnosis and treatment for many women."Black women die at a 40% higher rate [from breast cancer] than White women," Brem noted, and women with fewer resources have less access to mammograms. Brem wants to change this with her foundation, which for the past 20 years has championed early detection through innovative screening, increased education and awareness, and equitable access."I look forward to the more wide-reaching implementation of AI to help not only find more cancers, but with healthcare," she said.A breast cancer breath test?Brem is helping to develop a breath test that could detect breast cancer. "It's not available yet, but I'm really excited about having no pain, no compression, and no injection way of diagnosing if you're accurately diagnosed," Brem said. And there's hope it could someday help beyond breast cancer. "The next step on our roadmap is not just breast cancer but a women's health panel where you could do one breath and get all these tests done," Brem said. The current state of breast cancer screeningThe guidelines from the American College of Physicians stated in 2026 that women over the age of 50 should get a mammogram every other year. The United States Preventive Services Task Force recommends that women should start screening every other year at the age of 40. To Brem, "This is a travesty.""Women will die if they listen to that."From her research, women should get checked for breast cancer annually starting at the age of 40. For those with a history of breast cancer in their family, they should start at 35.This is all easier said than done. Women often cite anxiety as a reason they delay or skip getting screened. The thought of receiving a positive test result understandably makes women nervous, but as Brem notes, "We don't get rid of the disease by not knowing we have it."Early detection of breast cancer leads to significantly better outcomes compared to cases where breast cancer is found in its later stages. "Ninety-nine percent of women with early breast cancer survive and thrive," Brem said, but this outcome can only be possible if women screen for it early and regularly.In addition to the recommended mammograms, Brem also believes "you absolutely, unequivocally definitely need more exams" if you have dense breasts. Half of women have dense breasts, and mammograms might not be able to pick up potentially deadly tumors hiding behind the tissue. Ultrasounds, MRIs or contrast-enhanced mammograms are necessary for those with dense breasts to get a complete view of their risks.Supplemental screening isn't always standard with some doctors. Brem advised that it is "really important" for women to insist that their doctors order these extra exams. The mammograms are not enough.Demand more, get educated, and "be badass"Brem is adamant in her belief that women can be proactive now to better their health and improve their breast cancer outcomes. For those under 40 who think they have time until they need to start screening for breast cancer, think again."You're not too young to have breast cancer," Brem warns.Having the conversation now about your plan for breast cancer screenings and seeking out additional exams is essential in early detection and better prognosis. "If you find it early, even if you're young, it's curable," Brem said.Rates of cancer are rising in younger women and awareness is the first step to being proactive about your health. Her foundation provides resources to educate women. Brem urges you to advocate for yourself at the doctor's office."We tell women to be badass," she said. It's what you deserve, and it's not a maybe."

The crypto market cap stood at $2.53 trillion last Wednesday. As of this morning, it has dropped to $2.25 trillion, with Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) testing $61,500 overnight before rebounding to $63K. There’s quite a few reasons for the market plunge. Strategy broke a years-long rule and sold Bitcoin for the first time in nearly four years, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs are now on their longest outflow streak ever. On top of that, $1.76 billion in leveraged positions got liquidated in 24 hours, and fresh U.S. strikes on Iran have rattled the fragile ceasefire that had been holding since April. Every major coin is now down double digits on the month. Below is the breakdown of how Bitcoin, Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) are performing right now. Bitcoin is showing the worst of the market downturn. The largest cryptocurrency by market cap is now trading at $63,436, down 3.2% in 24 hours and down 22.3% on the month. The bigger picture is even worse, with Bitcoin trading more than 50% below its $126,000 all-time high. Meanwhile, Ethereum and XRP are doing no better. ETH is trading at $1,768 after a 25.8% slide on the month, and XRP at $1.17 has hit a 15-week low, down 17.3% on the month. Both followed Bitcoin’s slide and ended up losing even more ground. Solana took the hardest single-day hit of the four cryptocurrencies. SOL is down 4.6% in 24 hours alone and 20.9% over the past month, now trading at $68.38. High-beta altcoins like Solana and XRP amplify Bitcoin’s moves, and on the way down, that means they fall steeper than the rest of the market. Beyond the price drops, the leverage washout was also ugly. $1.76 billion in leveraged positions got liquidated in 24 hours, with $1.50 billion of that from long positions getting forced out. Bitcoin took $773 million of the damage, Ethereum $482 million, and Solana $88 million. Traders went into this week heavily long, and the market punished them for it. For nearly four years, Strategy (the company formerly known as MicroStrategy) was the loudest voice in Bitcoin, telling everyone to buy and never sell. The company built its corporate identity around accumulation, stacking 843,706 BTC over five years and turning Michael Saylor into the face of the institutional bullish thesis on Bitcoin. On Monday, that changed. Strategy disclosed in an SEC 8-K filing on June 1 that it had sold 32 Bitcoin between May 26 and May 31 for $2.5 million, at an average price of $77,135. The amount represents 0.004% of the company’s holdings. That is not a number that moves markets on its own, but the signal it sent did. That said, this was actually not panic selling. Saylor pre-announced the move on May 5, telling investors that Strategy would probably sell some bitcoin to pay a dividend just to inoculate the market and send the message that “we did it.” The 32 BTC went to fund distributions on STRC, which is the company’s perpetual preferred stock. So, the whole sequence was planned and telegraphed for weeks. However, none of that planning protected the stock. MSTR fell nearly 6% on Monday, then dropped another 7% on Wednesday as Bitcoin slid below $62,000. Two Wall Street analysts called the sale economically immaterial, but the narrative break was the bigger damage. For years, the “Saylor never sells” rule had been one of the arguments for holding Bitcoin through volatility. But the recent sale has made that argument look weaker, and the timing came right in the middle of the Bitcoin ETF outflow streak and a macro shock. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs were already on a record streak when last week ended, and they have now extended it further. The 10-day outflow run that closed May has stretched to 13 trading days as of June 3, deepening what was already the longest withdrawal streak since the funds launched in January 2024. The structural bid that had supported Bitcoin through every previous selloff is now selling instead of buying. The pace has been intense. On June 3 alone, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $396.6 million, led by BlackRock’s IBIT at $342.3 million and Fidelity’s FBTC at $54.3 million. And the day before, outflows hit $519 million. Since May 20, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost over $3 billion in cumulative net outflows, or roughly 40,000 BTC by holdings. Bitcoin ETF assets under management have dropped from around $109 billion to $85 billion during the streak, marking a 22% decline in three weeks. Ethereum ETFs have run their own parallel bleed, posting their 17th consecutive outflow day on June 3, with cumulative net inflows shrinking to $11.24 billion. The selling is not only happening in ETFs either. According to on-chain data, whales holding between 10 and 10,000 Bitcoin sold roughly 25,000 BTC in the past week alone. So it’s not just an ETF problem, but a wider sell-off happening across the board. Macro conditions have only made things worse for crypto. Inflation came in at 3.8% year-over-year in April, the hottest reading since May 2023, while wholesale prices jumped 6%, the largest increase since December 2022. Energy prices are up 17.9% on the year and gasoline is up 28.4%, which has pushed real wages negative for the first time since 2023. The Federal Reserve’s response has been to hold. The April FOMC vote was 8-4 to keep rates at 3.50%-3.75%, marking the most dissents since 1992. Markets are now pricing a 68.8% probability of zero rate cuts in all of 2026, according to Polymarket . New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, sworn in on May 22, has not had time to establish his own approach yet, which adds even more uncertainty. Then on Tuesday, June 2, Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain, and the U.S. retaliated late that night with strikes on an Iranian military facility on Qeshm Island. Iranian drones hit Kuwait International Airport on Wednesday, killing one and injuring 63. Three days later, neither side has clarified whether the ceasefire still holds. The result keeps the inflation loop intact. WTI crude is at $94.99, and Brent at $97.07. The U.S. has drained 14% of its Strategic Petroleum Reserve trying to ease supply pressure. As long as oil stays at these levels, the Fed cannot cut, and as long as the Fed cannot cut, macro pressure will keep weighing on the crypto market. The selloff looks closer to capitulation than the start of a new leg down. Bitcoin tested $61,500 overnight and bounced, and that level is close to the 200-week moving average, which has held as support in past bear cycles. A 13-day ETF outflow streak, $1.76 billion in liquidations in a single day, and a narrative-breaking Strategy sale are the bearish drivers weighing on the market right now. But whether they mark a bottom or signal more downside is still unclear. Despite all that, there are a couple of events coming up this month that could change the bearish sentiment in the market. The next CPI release on June 10 will show whether inflation is cooling or staying sticky. Then the FOMC meeting on June 16-17 gives the first read on how Warsh sets policy and the updated dot plot. Prices for both bitcoin and ethereum opened higher than yesterday's open and back in line with Monday's open. However, bitcoin and ethereum are losing some of those gains this morning after a hotter-than-expected CPI report : The Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% in September , compared with expectations for 3.6%, and an acceleration from 3.4% in August. Month-over-month prices rose 0.6%, versus expectations for 0.5%. Stripping out volatile food and energy prices — the way the Fed likes to scrutinize underlying inflation — CPI rose 0.3% month over month, compared with expectations for 0.2%, holding the same level as August. The year-over-year rate was 2.6%, compared with expectations for 2.5%, and up from 2.4% in August. The odds of a Fed rate increase later this month have also shifted dramatically following today's CPI report. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, the Fed now has about a 50-50 chance of raising rates by 25 basis points, compared with earlier in the week, when the odds were near 80% that it wouldn't raise rates in October. The all-time low value for ethereum was $0.4209 on Oct. 21, 2015. Bitcoin, ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies are rapidly evolving. Follow the latest developments from Yahoo Finance and others here . You generally owe taxes when you sell cryptocurrency for more than you paid for it. This also applies when you exchange one digital asset for another. Converting bitcoin into ethereum, for example, isn't "just a trade" in the eyes of the IRS. It's a taxable event if the value changes. Crypto taxes aren't paid at the time of the transaction, but instead, they're reported on your tax return for the year in which the transaction took place. So, if you sold crypto for a profit at any point during 2025, that activity is reported when you file your 2025 return in early 2026. How much tax you pay depends on two main factors: Your overall taxable income and filing status Hold it for less than a year, and you'll usually face higher rates. Hold it longer, and the rates tend to be lower. This holding-period distinction matters more than most people realize. A few days can make a difference of as much as 17% or more — so timing matters. Crypto taxes aren't paid at the time of the transaction, but instead, they're reported on your tax return for the year in which the transaction took place. So, if you sold crypto for a profit at any point during 2025, that activity is reported when you file your 2025 return in early 2026.

Your overall taxable income and filing status
